result.proposed_fix: Bind each piece to its own pixels with a differential render instead of 'is there ink in the box'. After the DOM snapshot, apply a CSS Custom Highlight (CSS.highlights.set('uri-probe', new Highlight(...ranges)) with ::highlight(uri-probe){color:<probe colour A>}), take the in-memory screenshot, switch the highlight to probe colour B and take a second screenshot, then remove the highlight. The page DOM and page.content() stay unchanged. Keep a piece only if enough pixels inside its rectangles change between the two shots in the expected direction, in proportion to its character count; otherwise drop it as no_ink. Text that is clipped, covered, below its parent's background, masked or fill:none changes no pixels and is dropped, and decoy ink under or over it does not change. Batch the pieces into a few colour-coded groups to limit the number of screenshots, and fail closed when the adapter cannot take both shots or the highlight API is missing. Selected text needs the same differential (highlight on, selection's own paint as baseline). Add a self-contained Chromium regression test (page embedded in the test) with the five overlap payloads above, plus the existing R11/R12/R13 payloads and visible controls, with and without Ctrl+A, asserting no payload in FakeClient.bodies. Update docs/03 to drop the 'overlaps other ink' residual or state the exact remaining limits. If a second screenshot per ask is not acceptable, the alternative is an owner decision to stop sending DOM text and send only text read from the screenshot.
result.root_cause: Every version of the hidden-text defence checks a stand-in for 'this text is visible to the user' instead of the claim itself. Up to d029f60 it was a list of CSS hiding techniques in snapshot.js. At HEAD (D10) it is uri_assist/onscreen.py Screen.check, which keeps a piece of page text (text, selection or heading) when the screenshot shows enough contrast edges inside the piece's own client rectangles. That proves some ink is in the rectangle, not that the piece's own characters are drawn. The page controls what is painted under or over the hidden text's rectangle, so hidden text placed on visible text, borders or a pattern passes. The rectangles come from Range.getClientRects, which ignores paint order, masks and fill. While text is selected the browser repaints it in its highlight colours, and the in-page sameAsBackground rule only handles a solid background colour. Probe /tmp/uri_diag_D8 (real Chromium, HEAD snapshot.js, mk/grant(observe)/ask_and_wait with the real screenshot): ZNEG (z-index:-1 under the parent's white background over the parent's own line), SVGNONE (fill=none over a visible SVG text), MASKBOX (-webkit-mask-box-image box over a visible line), PEN (pointer-events:none white overlay carrying visible text) and STRIPE (z-index:-1 text under a striped background) are not visible in no_selection.png. All five reach FakeClient.bodies under 'On-screen text (pixel-checked)' with redactions {}. With Ctrl+A, ZNEG, MASKBOX, PEN and STRIPE also appear under 'Selected text (pixel-checked)' (twice each; SVGNONE dropped out), redactions {'no_ink': 4}.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: 2de591e (R10, +14 lines in snapshot.js), d5a9b41 (R11, +86) and d029f60 (R12, +125) each added rules for the techniques the reviewer had just named (clip, overflow ancestors, text-indent, elementFromPoint occlusion, opacity/filter, text-fill colour, clip-path shapes, masks, closed details). Their regression tests replay only those payloads, so the next reviewer found new techniques each round (R12, R13). fcfb465 (D10) moved to a screenshot check. Its test page (test_a0_d10_pixel_checked_text.py PAGE) puts every payload on blank white space, so nothing tests hidden text over other ink. The thresholds were tuned on that layout, and docs/03 lists 'hidden text whose rectangle overlaps other drawn ink passes' as a residual limit, although that is an open bypass of the boundary. None of the repairs bound the text that is sent to the pixels that are drawn.
